title: A Death at Low Tide
description: Ambrose Thorne lies dead at his desk on a tidal island, and five people in the house could have killed him. The sea holds the causeway shut until six, so you have one night to question them, search the rooms, and name the killer before they can walk away. The game keeps your clues and notebook, shows how steady and how trusting each suspect is, and draws a different killer, weapon, and hiding place every time you start.
prompt:
Rain hammers the windows of Cormorant House, and the lamp on the dead man's desk is still burning.

Cormorant House stands alone on Skerry Holm, a tidal island joined to the mainland by one stone causeway. The sea covered the causeway at eight o'clock, and it stays under water until six in the morning. An hour ago the storm brought down the telephone line. Nobody can leave the island tonight, and nobody can reach it.

You crossed at twenty to eight because Ambrose Thorne wrote asking you to come tonight, on a matter he could not put in a letter. You dined with his household and never got your private word. Over dinner he said he would set certain things right at breakfast. At a quarter past nine he went to his study and asked not to be disturbed.

At twenty past eleven Mrs. Moffat, the housekeeper, carried up his cocoa and found him. Now it is half past eleven, and you stand in the study doorway. Ambrose sits slumped forward over the desk blotter, one arm hanging, a brandy glass on its side near his hand. The lamp is lit. Nobody has touched him. From the doorway you cannot see what killed him.

Downstairs in the drawing room the other five wait: his nephew Julian, his secretary Edith Crane, Dr. Leonard Fisk, his business partner Vivian Lasker, and Mrs. Moffat herself. One of them did this. At six the police can cross the causeway, and so can the killer.

Mrs. Moffat stands on the landing behind you, the cocoa tray still shaking in her hands, waiting for you to tell her what happens now.

(When you are sure, type accuse and a name, for example "accuse Julian". You get one accusation.)
memory: Cormorant House on Skerry Holm, about 1934. The player is a private inquiry agent whom Ambrose Thorne, 68, owner of the Thorne & Lasker shipping line, asked to come tonight. Ambrose died at his desk at about ten o'clock. Mrs. Moffat found him at 11:20 pm. The causeway is under water until 6:00 am and the telephone line is down, so there are no police and no laboratory tonight. The five in the house are Julian Thorne, Edith Crane, Dr. Leonard Fisk, Vivian Lasker, and Agnes Moffat. One of them killed him. Inspector Hale crosses on foot at six. The truth of the case is in the narrator's sealed file.
authors_note: A fair-play country-house mystery of the 1930s. Keep the prose spare and exact. Give each room physical detail the player can search. Suspects speak in their own voices: they evade, interrupt, and lie as the sealed file allows. Show composure and trust through behavior, never by naming a number.
ai_instructions:
Write in second person, present tense. The player is the inquiry agent. End each reply at a point where the player decides what to do next. Never decide or speak for the player.

The mystery is fair. The sealed case file in the plot essentials is fact: play it exactly and never alter it to fit the player's theory. Reveal a fact only when the player's action would uncover it. Suspects answer in character and may lie as the file says. The player has one formal accusation, made by typing accuse and a name. Before it, nobody confesses to the murder, and the narration never hints who did it. Keep every mention of the time consistent with the clock note.

Every number in the state_delta block is a change, not a total.

Composure and trust belong to each suspect separately. An innocent suspect at cracking composure or confiding trust gives up their lesser secret and what they saw. The killer at cracking composure slips and contradicts their own story, but does not confess.

Add to player.clues only for a new solid fact. In the same reply, send player.case_notes as the whole notebook with that fact added at the end. If the notebook nears 600 characters, shorten older phrases instead of dropping them.

Set flags.household_gathered false when the player takes a suspect aside or the group scatters, and true when all five are back together in the drawing room.

Mark each milestone as it happens, using the id shown beside the goal. Mark milestones.case_closed only when a verdict note tells you to.

story_cards.name: Cormorant House
story_cards.keys: cormorant, drawing room, library, billiard, morning room, estate office, conservatory, kitchen, plate room, servants' stair, terrace, boathouse, cellar
story_cards.entry: Cormorant House is a granite house of three floors on Skerry Holm. The ground floor holds the drawing room, library, billiard room, morning room, estate office, and conservatory, with a garden door to the terrace and a path down to the boathouse. Ambrose's study, bedroom, and dressing room are on the first floor off the main stair. The kitchen, plate room, and cellar lie below, joined to every floor by the servants' stair.
story_cards.notes: Every room any of the 45 cases needs is named here, so the narrator never invents a layout that breaks a trail.

story_cards.name: The Causeway and the Tide
story_cards.entry: The causeway is a raised stone road that joins Skerry Holm to the mainland at low tide. Tonight the sea covered it at eight o'clock, and it clears at six in the morning. Until then nobody can cross, and the storm has cut the telephone line.
story_cards.notes: The deadline. The clock note in the script keeps the time.

story_cards.name: Ambrose Thorne
story_cards.entry: Ambrose Thorne, 68, owned the Thorne & Lasker shipping line and Cormorant House. He was a hard, private man who wrote to an inquiry agent rather than to his solicitor. At dinner tonight he said he would set certain things right at breakfast. At a quarter past nine he went to his study and asked not to be disturbed.
story_cards.notes: Public facts only. The breakfast line fits every killer's motive.

story_cards.name: The Study
story_cards.keys: study, desk, mantel, blotter, brandy, decanter, paper knife, tide clock
story_cards.entry: Ambrose Thorne's study is on the first floor. On an ordinary evening a brass tide clock stands on the mantel, a narrow paper knife lies in the desk tray, and a decanter of brandy sits on the side table. Anything missing or disturbed in the study tonight matters.
story_cards.notes: Worded as an ordinary evening, so it fits all three methods.

story_cards.name: Thorne & Lasker Line
story_cards.keys: shipping, the firm, ledger, accounts, company, steamer
story_cards.entry: The Thorne & Lasker Line runs cargo steamers out of the northern ports. Ambrose Thorne and Vivian Lasker own it together. This past year the talk on the quays is that money is short and the ships are old.
story_cards.notes: Background for the crane, lasker, and moffat motives without pointing at any one.

story_cards.name: Dr. Fisk's Bag
story_cards.keys: medical bag, doctor's bag, chloral, vial, sleeping draught, hall table
story_cards.entry: Dr. Fisk's medical bag stood on the hall table all evening, where anyone passing could reach it. It holds his instruments and several small vials of chloral hydrate, a sleeping draught that kills in a large dose.
story_cards.notes: Needed for the poison method. True in every case.

story_cards.name: Inspector Hale
story_cards.entry: Inspector Hale of the county police is expected to cross the causeway on foot at six. He is thorough and unhurried, and he will search the whole house. Until he arrives, the inquiry agent is the only investigator on Skerry Holm.
story_cards.notes: Arrives at dawn in the script's turn-18 note and in the endings.

scripts.name: The Sealed Case
scripts.description: Draws a killer, a method, and a hiding place when the adventure starts, gives the narrator the same sealed answer every turn, keeps the night's clock, and judges the one formal accusation.
